e-5577.problem: Find a matrix that defines the orthogonal projection of $\mathbb{R}^3$ onto the subspace spanned by ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14071876/assets/16f06043e1f8bcab11a7e43fc76800c33e2560bb00e425c9c88f8cfeb8c12ee3.png)
e-5577.worked_solution:
Recall that the matrix $P_S = A(A^T\!A)^{-1}\!A^T$ maps any vector $\mathbf x\in \mathbb{R}^n$ onto its orthogonal projection in the subspace $S$ spanned by the columns of the matrix $A.$ 

In our case, ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14071876/assets/fde70db50cff408347bdebc086fbfa3ae87020bb0300b32dad67168d617ed607.png) Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{S} & =A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -3\end{aligned}]{([\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -3\end{aligned}])}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -3\end{aligned}]\cdot (14)^{-1}[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{14}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -3\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{14}[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -3 \\ 2 & 4 & -6 \\ -3 & -6 & 9\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

e-8316.knowledge_point: Finding a Matrix That Defines an Orthogonal Projection Onto the Subspace Spanned by a Plane
e-8316.problem:
Find a matrix that defines the orthogonal projection of $\mathbb{R}^3$ onto the plane whose parametric equation is $\mathbf{r}=s\mathbf{v} + t\mathbf{w}$, where
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14071876/assets/bd8680b251ca871c0912f7aa85826bc705f022d12155fa1ddc73e2d01c30d2ca.png)
e-8316.worked_solution:
Recall that the matrix $P_S = A(A^T\!A)^{-1}\!A^T$ maps any vector $\mathbf x\in \mathbb{R}^n$ onto its orthogonal projection in the subspace $S$ spanned by the columns of the matrix $A.$ 

Notice that the plane $\mathbf{r}=s\mathbf{v}+t\mathbf{w}$ is actually the subspace $\text{Span}\{\mathbf{v}, \mathbf{w}\}.$ 
Hence, we have 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14071876/assets/af442d03acdc13db51c3ae53fcf250074e9adc2d4ed4bd2f52e6e76b5d4c2fe8.png)

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{S} & =A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]{([\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}])}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]{[\begin{aligned}6 & 0 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{6}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{6}[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 1 \\ 2 & -2 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

e-5578.problem:
Which of the following are orthogonal projection matrices?

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14071876/assets/5b3093e1c65624c862d949706ed5922ab8078beac752d4e7347c71be993580d8.png)
e-5578.worked_solution:
Recall that $Q$ is an orthogonal projection matrix if and only if $Q^2=Q$ and $Q^T=Q.$ 

With that in mind, let's examine our matrices.

- $A$ is *not* an orthogonal projection matrix. We have
$A^T = A$
but 

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{2} & =A\cdot A \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 & 5 \\ 5 & 10\end{aligned}] \\  & \ne A.\end{aligned}
$$

- $B$ is *not* an orthogonal projection matrix. We have

$$
\begin{aligned}{B}^{T}\ne B.\end{aligned}
$$

- $C$ is an orthogonal projection matrix. Indeed,
$C^T = C$
and

$$
\begin{aligned}{C}^{2} & =C\cdot C \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{4}{5} & \frac{2}{5} \\ \frac{2}{5} & \frac{1}{5}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}\frac{4}{5} & \frac{2}{5} \\ \frac{2}{5} & \frac{1}{5}\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}4 & 2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}4 & 2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{25}[\begin{aligned}4 & 2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 & 2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{25}[\begin{aligned}20 & 10 \\ 10 & 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{4}{5} & \frac{2}{5} \\ \frac{2}{5} & \frac{1}{5}\end{aligned}] \\  & =C.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "$C$ only."

Question 1

Find a matrix that defines the orthogonal projection of R3 onto the subspace spanned by a=[324].

a
129[36126481282]
b
129[961264812816]
c
129[912612486816]
d
13[46126381282]
e
119[961264812816]
Submit

decision.explanation: The projection matrix is P=aa^T/(a^Ta). Here a^Ta=3^2+2^2+4^2=29 and aa^T has rows (9,6,12), (6,4,8), and (12,8,16), giving option b.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem: Find a matrix that defines the orthogonal projection of ${R}^{3}$ onto the subspace spanned by $a=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2 \\ 4\end{aligned}].$
after.worked_solution:
Recall that the matrix ${P}_{S}=A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T}$ maps any vector $x\in {R}^{n}$ onto its orthogonal projection in the subspace $S$ spanned by the columns of the matrix $A.$ 

In our case, $A=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2 \\ 4\end{aligned}].$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{S} & =A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2 \\ 4\end{aligned}]{([\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2 \\ 4\end{aligned}])}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}] \\  & ={29}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2 \\ 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{29}[\begin{aligned}9 & 6 & 12 \\ 6 & 4 & 8 \\ 12 & 8 & 16\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Find a matrix that defines the orthogonal projection of R3 onto the subspace spanned by a=[324].

EXPLANATION

Recall that the matrix PS=A(ATA)−1AT maps any vector x∈Rn onto its orthogonal projection in the subspace S spanned by the columns of the matrix A.

In our case, A=[324]. Therefore,

PS=A(ATA)−1AT=[324]([324][324])−1[324]=29−1[324][324]=129[961264812816].

content.knowledge_point: Finding a Matrix that Defines an Orthogonal Projection Onto the Subspace Spanned by a Vector
content.problem: Find a matrix that defines the orthogonal projection of ${R}^{3}$ onto the subspace spanned by $a=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2 \\ 4\end{aligned}].$
content.worked_solution:
Recall that the matrix ${P}_{S}=A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T}$ maps any vector $x\in {R}^{n}$ onto its orthogonal projection in the subspace $S$ spanned by the columns of the matrix $A.$ 

In our case, $A=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2 \\ 4\end{aligned}].$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{S} & =A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2 \\ 4\end{aligned}]{([\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2 \\ 4\end{aligned}])}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}] \\  & ={29}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2 \\ 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{29}[\begin{aligned}9 & 6 & 12 \\ 6 & 4 & 8 \\ 12 & 8 & 16\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Question 2
?

Find a matrix that defines the orthogonal projection of R3 onto the subspace spanned by a=[412].

a
17[824212424]
b
121[412124244]
c
17[412824428]
d
120[412124248]
e
121[1648412824]
Submit

decision.explanation: The orthogonal projection matrix is P=aa^T/(a^Ta). Since a^Ta=4^2+1^2+2^2=21, the outer product aa^T gives rows (16,4,8), (4,1,2), and (8,2,4). Thus option e is correct.

after.name: Question 2
after.problem: Find a matrix that defines the orthogonal projection of ${R}^{3}$ onto the subspace spanned by $a=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$
after.worked_solution:
Recall that the matrix ${P}_{S}=A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T}$ maps any vector $x\in {R}^{n}$ onto its orthogonal projection in the subspace $S$ spanned by the columns of the matrix $A.$ 

In our case, $A=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{S} & =A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]{([\begin{aligned}4 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}])}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}4 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =(21)^{-1}[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{21}[\begin{aligned}16 & 4 & 8 \\ 4 & 1 & 2 \\ 8 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Finding a Matrix that Defines an Orthogonal Projection Onto the Subspace Spanned by a Vector
content.problem: Find a matrix that defines the orthogonal projection of ${R}^{3}$ onto the subspace spanned by $a=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$
content.worked_solution:
Recall that the matrix ${P}_{S}=A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T}$ maps any vector $x\in {R}^{n}$ onto its orthogonal projection in the subspace $S$ spanned by the columns of the matrix $A.$ 

In our case, $A=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{S} & =A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]{([\begin{aligned}4 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}])}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}4 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =(21)^{-1}[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{21}[\begin{aligned}16 & 4 & 8 \\ 4 & 1 & 2 \\ 8 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Question 3
?

Find a matrix that defines the orthogonal projection of R3 onto the subspace spanned by a=[20−1].

a
15[40−2201000]
b
15[10−200020−1]
c
15[40−220−1−201]
d
15[40−2000−201]
e
5[−201201000]
Submit

decision.explanation: The orthogonal projection matrix is P=aa^T/(a^Ta). Here a^Ta=2^2+0^2+(-1)^2=5, and aa^T has rows (4,0,-2), (0,0,0), and (-2,0,1). This matches option d.

after.name: Question 3
after.problem: Find a matrix that defines the orthogonal projection of ${R}^{3}$ onto the subspace spanned by $a=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{aligned}].$
after.worked_solution:
Recall that the matrix ${P}_{S}=A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T}$ maps any vector $x\in {R}^{n}$ onto its orthogonal projection in the subspace $S$ spanned by the columns of the matrix $A.$ 

In our case, $A=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{aligned}].$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{S} & =A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{aligned}]{([\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{aligned}])}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =(5)^{-1}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Question 3
?

Find a matrix that defines the orthogonal projection of R3 onto the subspace spanned by a=[20−1].

a
15[40−2201000]
b
15[10−200020−1]
c
15[40−220−1−201]
d
15[40−2000−201]
e
5[−201201000]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Recall that the matrix PS=A(ATA)−1AT maps any vector x∈Rn onto its orthogonal projection in the subspace S spanned by the columns of the matrix A.

In our case, A=[20−1]. Therefore,

PS=A(ATA)−1AT=[20−1]([20−1][20−1])−1[20−1]=(5)−1[20−1][20−1]=15[40−2000−201].

content.knowledge_point: Finding a Matrix that Defines an Orthogonal Projection Onto the Subspace Spanned by a Vector
content.problem: Find a matrix that defines the orthogonal projection of ${R}^{3}$ onto the subspace spanned by $a=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{aligned}].$
content.worked_solution:
Recall that the matrix ${P}_{S}=A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T}$ maps any vector $x\in {R}^{n}$ onto its orthogonal projection in the subspace $S$ spanned by the columns of the matrix $A.$ 

In our case, $A=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{aligned}].$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{S} & =A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{aligned}]{([\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{aligned}])}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =(5)^{-1}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

before.html:
Question 4
?

Find a matrix that defines the orthogonal projection of R3 onto the subspace spanned by a=[5−21].

a
130[25−105−104−25−21]
b
15[5−21−25−21−21]
c
13[25−105−104−25−21]
d
130[5−1025−104−225−21]
e
130[10−255−254−325−321]
Submit

decision.explanation: The projection matrix is P=aa^T/(a^Ta). Here a^Ta=25+4+1=30, and aa^T has rows (25,-10,5), (-10,4,-2), and (5,-2,1), matching option a.

after.name: Question 4
after.problem: Find a matrix that defines the orthogonal projection of ${R}^{3}$ onto the subspace spanned by $a=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$
after.worked_solution:
Recall that the matrix ${P}_{S}=A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T}$ maps any vector $x\in {R}^{n}$ onto its orthogonal projection in the subspace $S$ spanned by the columns of the matrix $A.$ 

In our case, $A=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{S} & =A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{([\begin{aligned}5 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}5 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}])}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}5 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={30}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}5 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{30}[\begin{aligned}25 & -10 & 5 \\ -10 & 4 & -2 \\ 5 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Question 4

Find a matrix that defines the orthogonal projection of R3 onto the subspace spanned by a=[5−21].

a
130[25−105−104−25−21]
b
15[5−21−25−21−21]
c
13[25−105−104−25−21]
d
130[5−1025−104−225−21]
e
130[10−255−254−325−321]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Recall that the matrix PS=A(ATA)−1AT maps any vector x∈Rn onto its orthogonal projection in the subspace S spanned by the columns of the matrix A.

In our case, A=[5−21]. Therefore,

PS=A(ATA)−1AT=[5−21]([5−21][5−21])−1[5−21]=30−1[5−21][5−21]=130[25−105−104−25−21].

verification.explanation: The revealed solution confirms option a. The projection is aa^T/(a^Ta), where a^Ta=25+4+1=30 and aa^T has rows (25,-10,5), (-10,4,-2), and (5,-2,1). The incorrect submission selected b.

content.knowledge_point: Finding a Matrix that Defines an Orthogonal Projection Onto the Subspace Spanned by a Vector
content.problem: Find a matrix that defines the orthogonal projection of ${R}^{3}$ onto the subspace spanned by $a=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$
content.worked_solution:
Recall that the matrix ${P}_{S}=A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T}$ maps any vector $x\in {R}^{n}$ onto its orthogonal projection in the subspace $S$ spanned by the columns of the matrix $A.$ 

In our case, $A=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{S} & =A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{([\begin{aligned}5 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}5 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}])}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}5 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={30}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}5 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{30}[\begin{aligned}25 & -10 & 5 \\ -10 & 4 & -2 \\ 5 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

before.html:
Question 5
?

Find a matrix that defines the orthogonal projection of R3 onto the subspace spanned by a=[3−21].

a
 14[9−43−44−13−11]
b
 114[9−63−64−23−21]
c
 114[1−69−642921]
d
 17[6−33−33−43−41]
e
 114[1−24−296463]
Submit

decision.explanation: The projection matrix is P=aa^T/(a^Ta). Here a^Ta=9+4+1=14, and aa^T has rows (9,-6,3), (-6,4,-2), and (3,-2,1), matching option b.

after.name: Question 5
after.problem: Find a matrix that defines the orthogonal projection of ${R}^{3}$ onto the subspace spanned by $a=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$
after.worked_solution:
Recall that the matrix ${P}_{S}=A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T}$ maps any vector $x\in {R}^{n}$ onto its orthogonal projection in the subspace $S$ spanned by the columns of the matrix $A.$ 

In our case, $A=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{S} & =A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{([\begin{aligned}3 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}])}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =(14)^{-1}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{14}[\begin{aligned}9 & -6 & 3 \\ -6 & 4 & -2 \\ 3 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Find a matrix that defines the orthogonal projection of R3 onto the subspace spanned by a=[3−21].

a
 14[9−43−44−13−11]
b
 114[9−63−64−23−21]
c
 114[1−69−642921]
d
 17[6−33−33−43−41]
e
 114[1−24−296463]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Recall that the matrix PS=A(ATA)−1AT maps any vector x∈Rn onto its orthogonal projection in the subspace S spanned by the columns of the matrix A.

In our case, A=[3−21]. Therefore,

PS=A(ATA)−1AT=[3−21]([3−21][3−21])−1[3−21]=(14)−1[3−21][3−21]=114[9−63−64−23−21].

content.knowledge_point: Finding a Matrix that Defines an Orthogonal Projection Onto the Subspace Spanned by a Vector
content.problem: Find a matrix that defines the orthogonal projection of ${R}^{3}$ onto the subspace spanned by $a=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$
content.worked_solution:
Recall that the matrix ${P}_{S}=A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T}$ maps any vector $x\in {R}^{n}$ onto its orthogonal projection in the subspace $S$ spanned by the columns of the matrix $A.$ 

In our case, $A=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{S} & =A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{([\begin{aligned}3 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}])}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =(14)^{-1}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{14}[\begin{aligned}9 & -6 & 3 \\ -6 & 4 & -2 \\ 3 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: The vectors span the plane x=z: v+w=(0,2,0) and v-w=(2,0,2). Orthogonal projection sends (x,y,z) to ((x+z)/2,y,(x+z)/2), whose matrix is option d.

after.name: Question 6
after.problem:
Find a matrix that defines the orthogonal projection of ${R}^{3}$ onto the plane whose parametric equation is $r=sv+tw$, where

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,w=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}].
$$
after.worked_solution:
Recall that the matrix ${P}_{S}=A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T}$ maps any vector $x\in {R}^{n}$ onto its orthogonal projection in the subspace $S$ spanned by the columns of the matrix $A.$ 

Notice that the plane $r=sv+tw$ is actually the subspace $\text{Span}{v,w}.$ 
Hence, we have 

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{S} & =A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}]{([\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 \\ -1 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}])}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 \\ -1 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}]{[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 \\ -1 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{8}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 \\ -1 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{8}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 4 & 2 \\ -2 & 4 & -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Finding a Matrix That Defines an Orthogonal Projection Onto the Subspace Spanned by a Plane
content.problem:
Find a matrix that defines the orthogonal projection of ${R}^{3}$ onto the plane whose parametric equation is $r=sv+tw$, where

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,w=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}].
$$
content.worked_solution:
Recall that the matrix ${P}_{S}=A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T}$ maps any vector $x\in {R}^{n}$ onto its orthogonal projection in the subspace $S$ spanned by the columns of the matrix $A.$ 

Notice that the plane $r=sv+tw$ is actually the subspace $\text{Span}{v,w}.$ 
Hence, we have 

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{S} & =A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}]{([\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 \\ -1 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}])}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 \\ -1 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}]{[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 \\ -1 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{8}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 \\ -1 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{8}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 4 & 2 \\ -2 & 4 & -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 7
after.problem:
Find a matrix that defines the orthogonal projection of ${R}^{3}$ onto the plane whose parametric equation is $r=sv+tw$, where

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,w=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 3\end{aligned}].
$$
after.worked_solution:
Recall that the matrix ${P}_{S}=A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T}$ maps any vector $x\in {R}^{n}$ onto its orthogonal projection in the subspace $S$ spanned by the columns of the matrix $A.$ 

Notice that the plane $r=sv+tw$ is actually the subspace $\text{Span}{v,w}.$ 
Hence, we have 

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -1 & 2 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{S} & =A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -1 & 2 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}]{([\begin{aligned}0 & -1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -1 & 2 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}])}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -1 & 2 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}]{[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 1 & 14\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{27}[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -1 & 2 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}14 & -1 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & -1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{27}[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -1 & 2 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 & -16 & 11 \\ 2 & 5 & 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{27}[\begin{aligned}2 & 5 & 5 \\ 5 & 26 & -1 \\ 5 & -1 & 26\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Finding a Matrix That Defines an Orthogonal Projection Onto the Subspace Spanned by a Plane
content.problem:
Find a matrix that defines the orthogonal projection of ${R}^{3}$ onto the plane whose parametric equation is $r=sv+tw$, where

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,w=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 3\end{aligned}].
$$
content.worked_solution:
Recall that the matrix ${P}_{S}=A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T}$ maps any vector $x\in {R}^{n}$ onto its orthogonal projection in the subspace $S$ spanned by the columns of the matrix $A.$ 

Notice that the plane $r=sv+tw$ is actually the subspace $\text{Span}{v,w}.$ 
Hence, we have 

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -1 & 2 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{S} & =A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -1 & 2 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}]{([\begin{aligned}0 & -1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -1 & 2 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}])}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -1 & 2 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}]{[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 1 & 14\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{27}[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -1 & 2 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}14 & -1 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & -1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{27}[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -1 & 2 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 & -16 & 11 \\ 2 & 5 & 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{27}[\begin{aligned}2 & 5 & 5 \\ 5 & 26 & -1 \\ 5 & -1 & 26\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: A normal vector is n=(2,-2,1), perpendicular to both given vectors, with n^Tn=9. The orthogonal projection is P=I−nn^T/9, which gives option a.

after.name: Question 8
after.problem:
Find a matrix that defines the orthogonal projection of ${R}^{3}$ onto the plane whose parametric equation is $r=sv+tw$, where

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,w=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$
after.worked_solution:
Recall that the matrix ${P}_{S}=A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T}$ maps any vector $x\in {R}^{n}$ onto its orthogonal projection in the subspace $S$ spanned by the columns of the matrix $A.$ 

Notice that the plane $r=sv+tw$ is actually the subspace $\text{Span}{v,w}.$ 
Hence, we have 

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \\ 2 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{S} & =A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \\ 2 & 2\end{aligned}]{([\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \\ 2 & 2\end{aligned}])}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \\ 2 & 2\end{aligned}]{[\begin{aligned}5 & 4 \\ 4 & 5\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{9}[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \\ 2 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}5 & -4 \\ -4 & 5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{9}[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \\ 2 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-5 & -4 & 2 \\ 4 & 5 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{9}[\begin{aligned}5 & 4 & -2 \\ 4 & 5 & 2 \\ -2 & 2 & 8\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Finding a Matrix That Defines an Orthogonal Projection Onto the Subspace Spanned by a Plane
content.problem:
Find a matrix that defines the orthogonal projection of ${R}^{3}$ onto the plane whose parametric equation is $r=sv+tw$, where

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,w=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$
content.worked_solution:
Recall that the matrix ${P}_{S}=A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T}$ maps any vector $x\in {R}^{n}$ onto its orthogonal projection in the subspace $S$ spanned by the columns of the matrix $A.$ 

Notice that the plane $r=sv+tw$ is actually the subspace $\text{Span}{v,w}.$ 
Hence, we have 

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \\ 2 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{S} & =A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \\ 2 & 2\end{aligned}]{([\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \\ 2 & 2\end{aligned}])}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \\ 2 & 2\end{aligned}]{[\begin{aligned}5 & 4 \\ 4 & 5\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{9}[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \\ 2 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}5 & -4 \\ -4 & 5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{9}[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \\ 2 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-5 & -4 & 2 \\ 4 & 5 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{9}[\begin{aligned}5 & 4 & -2 \\ 4 & 5 & 2 \\ -2 & 2 & 8\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: A normal vector is n=v×w=(-3,5,1), with n^Tn=35. The orthogonal projection matrix P=I−nn^T/35 has rows (26,15,3), (15,10,-5), and (3,-5,34), all divided by 35. This matches option b.

after.name: Question 9
after.problem:
Find a matrix that defines the orthogonal projection of ${R}^{3}$ onto the plane whose parametric equation is $r=sv+tw$, where

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,w=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ -2\end{aligned}].
$$
after.worked_solution:
Recall that the matrix ${P}_{S}=A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T}$ maps any vector $x\in {R}^{n}$ onto its orthogonal projection in the subspace $S$ spanned by the columns of the matrix $A.$ 

Notice that the plane $r=sv+tw$ is actually the subspace $\text{Span}{v,w}.$ 
Hence, we have 

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{S} & =A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}]{([\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}])}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}]{[\begin{aligned}6 & 1 \\ 1 & 6\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{35}[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}6 & -1 \\ -1 & 6\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{35}[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}11 & 5 & 8 \\ 4 & 5 & -13\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{35}[\begin{aligned}26 & 15 & 3 \\ 15 & 10 & -5 \\ 3 & -5 & 34\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Finding a Matrix That Defines an Orthogonal Projection Onto the Subspace Spanned by a Plane
content.problem:
Find a matrix that defines the orthogonal projection of ${R}^{3}$ onto the plane whose parametric equation is $r=sv+tw$, where

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,w=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ -2\end{aligned}].
$$
content.worked_solution:
Recall that the matrix ${P}_{S}=A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T}$ maps any vector $x\in {R}^{n}$ onto its orthogonal projection in the subspace $S$ spanned by the columns of the matrix $A.$ 

Notice that the plane $r=sv+tw$ is actually the subspace $\text{Span}{v,w}.$ 
Hence, we have 

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{S} & =A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}]{([\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}])}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}]{[\begin{aligned}6 & 1 \\ 1 & 6\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{35}[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}6 & -1 \\ -1 & 6\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{35}[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}11 & 5 & 8 \\ 4 & 5 & -13\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{35}[\begin{aligned}26 & 15 & 3 \\ 15 & 10 & -5 \\ 3 & -5 & 34\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: A normal vector is n=(1,-2,1), perpendicular to both v and w, with n^Tn=6. Thus the orthogonal projection P=I−nn^T/6 equals option c.

after.name: Question 10
after.problem:
Find a matrix that defines the orthogonal projection of ${R}^{3}$ onto the plane whose parametric equation is $r=sv+tw$, where

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,w=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$
after.worked_solution:
Recall that the matrix ${P}_{S}=A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T}$ maps any vector $x\in {R}^{n}$ onto its orthogonal projection in the subspace $S$ spanned by the columns of the matrix $A.$ 

Notice that the plane $r=sv+tw$ is actually the subspace $\text{Span}{v,w}.$ 
Hence, we have 

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{S} & =A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]{([\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}])}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]{[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{6}[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{6}[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-3 & 0 & 3 \\ 2 & 2 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{6}[\begin{aligned}5 & 2 & -1 \\ 2 & 2 & 2 \\ -1 & 2 & 5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Finding a Matrix That Defines an Orthogonal Projection Onto the Subspace Spanned by a Plane
content.problem:
Find a matrix that defines the orthogonal projection of ${R}^{3}$ onto the plane whose parametric equation is $r=sv+tw$, where

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,w=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$
content.worked_solution:
Recall that the matrix ${P}_{S}=A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T}$ maps any vector $x\in {R}^{n}$ onto its orthogonal projection in the subspace $S$ spanned by the columns of the matrix $A.$ 

Notice that the plane $r=sv+tw$ is actually the subspace $\text{Span}{v,w}.$ 
Hence, we have 

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore,

$$

$$
